title: Southern Crab Nebula
caption: The Southern Crab Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Southern Crab Nebula; He2-104 · constellation Centaurus · about 10,700 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A colorful hourglass shape spreads out from a bright white star, with a glowing figure eight at its center. This is the Southern Crab Nebula, officially Hen 2-104, about 10,700 light-years away in the southern constellation Centaurus. Hubble took the image to mark its 29th launch anniversary.

The nebula has two nested hourglasses, shaped by a pair of stars orbiting each other, an ageing red giant and a white dwarf. As the giant sheds its outer layers, the white dwarf's gravity pulls in some of that material, so both stars sit inside a flat disk of gas. The disk pinches the outflow so gas escapes only above and below it.

The bubbles are brightest at their edges, which makes them look like crab legs. These are likely where the outflow strikes surrounding gas and dust. The outer structure may be only thousands of years old, and the inner hourglass is more recent. Eventually the red giant will collapse into a white dwarf, and the two white dwarfs will light up a planetary nebula.

understand.summary: Hubble's WFC3 took this image through narrow filters. NASA shows F502N in blue, F656N in orange, F658N in green and F673N in red.
understand.eye: Narrow filters isolate light from individual glowing gases, and the colors are assigned to bring out the nebula's chemistry rather than to match what an eye would see.

explore: First reported in the late 1960s, the object was at first taken for an ordinary star. Astronomers using ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile photographed a roughly crab-shaped nebula in 1989, and Hubble revealed the nested structures in 1999. The colors trace glowing gases, with red marking sulfur and blue marking oxygen.
